title: Runtime occupancy projection for holistic kernel matching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Build a runtime component that projects short-horizon GPU occupancy and matches kernels holistically to expected occupancy + sequence-length profile, instead of using static per-operation heuristics. Motivation: current kernel selection uses per-op latency/throughput fingerprints that assume a stable occupancy and batch mix. In mixed workloads with frequent microbursts and diverse seq-len distributions, those heuristics mis-predict tail latency and result in suboptimal kernel choices that either inflate cost or violate latency SLOs. This work introduces a lightweight occupancy projection model, an occupancy-aware kernel scoring function, and a soft-hedging fallback plan to reduce p95/p99 latency regressions while preserving unit cost.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Offline simulator shows >= 15% reduction in simulated p99 under mixed bursts for two target models (Llama2-13B and MPT-7B) across three seq-len mixes. 2) Runtime A/B on staging demonstrates p95/p99 reduction without >5% regression in mean token cost. 3) Feature flag rollout to 10% of production; metrics (kernel fallback rate, occupancy projection error, tail latency) have dashboards and alerting. 4) No increase in error-rate or incorrect model outputs; no data leakage. 5) All PRs have tests and perf microbenchmarks recorded in CI artifacts.
implementation_notes:
Design:
- Input signals: incoming request metadata (model id, route, token budget, estimated prefill length), recent dispatch telemetry (batch sizes, active contexts, KV cache occupancy), and host-level GPU counters (smoothed SM utilization, memory used, queued tasks).
- Occupancy projection: short-timescale autoregressive predictor (lightweight exponential smoothing + categorical adjustment by model/route) to predict occupancy over the next 500ms window.
- Kernel scoring: combine expected latency under predicted occupancy and seq-len distribution with a stability penalty (switch cost) and fallback hedging cost. Score = alpha*latency + beta*cost + gamma*switch_penalty + delta*fallback_risk.
- Hedging: pick primary kernel but warm a fallback kernel (quantized/alternative attention implementation) if projection confidence low or microburst probability high. Fallback warmup is limited to small helper lanes to avoid capacity blowouts.
- Probe policy: for unseen model/seqlen combinations run a bounded prefill micro-probe (fast single-request microbenchmark) to calibrate scores.
- Feature flag and rollout: implement behind runtime flag, start on staging, then canary 10% traffic, measure metrics.

Implementation steps:
1) Simulator: extend existing kernel-sim to accept occupancy traces and evaluate scoring function. (2 weeks)
2) Instrumentation: add minimal telemetry events for occupancy features and probe outcomes. (1 week)
3) Scoring module & probe implement: prototype in Rust runtime with FFI hooks. (2 weeks)
4) Staging rollout + dashboards: configure dashboards, alerts, and run experiments. (1 week)
5) Gradual production rollout with monitoring. (2 weeks)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Occupancy projection errors cause unnecessary kernel flips and degrade latency. Mitigation: conservative confidence threshold for switches; use switch_penalty in score; require multi-sample corroboration before switching for hot paths. Risk: Warm hedging consumes capacity and increases cost. Mitigation: cap hedging warmers per GPU and evict based on least-recently-used route; monitor hedging rate and unit cost. Risk: Implementation complexity in runtime path could add overhead. Mitigation: keep predictor computation O(1) per decision and cache results for short windows; microbench to bound added latency.
telemetry_requirements: Emit the following lightweight events: occupancy_projection{model,route,predicted_window_ms,predicted_occupancy,confidence}, kernel_choice{model,route,kernel_id,score_components}, fallback_warm_start{kernel_id,trigger_reason}, probe_result{model,seq_len,latency_us,kernel_id}, kernel_switch_event{from,to,reason,latency_change}. Add histogram metrics for p50/p90/p95/p99 per route per kernel, occupancy_projection_error (absolute %), and hedging_warmers_active_count. These should feed a new dashboard 'occupancy-kernel-matching' and supporting alerts (p99 increased >10% relative to baseline, projection_error > 30% sustained for 5m, hedging_rate > 2% of requests).
experiments: Offline: run workloads mixing conversational short-turns, long-document prefill, and streaming decode bursts. Sweep alpha/beta/gamma/delta to find Pareto frontier for latency vs cost. Live: A/B compare default selector vs occupancy-matching on staging for 48h with synthetic microburst injection and real traffic shadow. Canary: 10% traffic with aggressive monitoring and automatic rollback on tail SLA breaches.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and projection smoothing. Integration tests in runtime-local runbook to validate fallback hedging does not over-allocate. Add microbench jobs to CI that run kernel comparisons under mocked occupancy traces. Include a chaos test that injects sudden 3x occupancy spikes and assert fallback behaves correctly.
rollout_plan: 1) Staging feature flag on (full synthetic load) -> verify metrics. 2) Canary 10% prod for 24-72h -> auto rollback if alerts fire. 3) 50% for 48h -> observe cost and tail. 4) 100% if stable.
related_notes: Prefer scoring abstraction to remain composable with policy-based routing (cost-tier fallback).
Avoid changing attention kernel implementations in this ticket; this focuses on selection layer only.
